newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish shares dive on fresh political concerns.
newsitem.headline: Turkish shares dive on fresh political concerns.

text.p: Turkish shares dropped heavily in active afternoon selling on a wave of concern about the future of the country's Islamist-led government, with the drop exacerbated by negative technical factors, dealers said.
The IMKB National-100 index declined 4.49 percent, or 71 points to close at 1,511 after dipping to an intraday low of 1,480 in late trading. The index was little changed at midday.

A nervous bout of selling in the afternoon sent daily trading volume up to 27.51 trillion lira ($216 million) from Wednesday's 19.75 trillion. The downtrend accelerated after a break through key support at 1,550.
"We are completely indexed to politics. We cannot expect a move upwards while there is the thought in people's heads that there might be a crisis," said Huseyin Istanbullu of Meksa Securities.
"In particular the statements made by (Health Minister Yildirim) Aktuna influenced the market negatively," he said.

Aktuna, from the conservative wing of Turkey's coalition government said on Thursday he was not hopeful that the ruling Islamist Welfare Party (RP) would support measures to crack down on Islam-based activism.
"Personally, I am certainly not hopeful about RP. I do not think they will show understanding and be helpful to us," Aktuna was quoted as saying by state-run Anatolian news agency.
Turkey's military-dominated National Security Council (NSC) last month issued a series of orders aimed at stemming the rising prominence of Islamist activities in public life.
"For RP to accept the NSC decisions means giving up the policies which they have followed until today," Aktuna said.

Dealers forecast that further declines were possible unless action was taken to calm the political concerns. Political uncertainty has unsettled shares trading in the wake of a strong rally in the first two months of the year which lifted the index around 60 percent in lira terms on hopes for privatisation.

"This fall was an indication of the poor state of the market. If it is the report of negative political news a 1,450 point level will be seen and it will continue like this," said Koray Cervatoglu of Baran Securities.
Share prices were also depressed by market speculation that the minister Aktuna would resign. After the close of trading Aktuna told Reuters he had no intention of doing so.

Dealers said the statements by Aktuna added to expectations of increased discord within the nine-month-old coalition of Islamist Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan over plans to raise compulsory state education to eight years from five in line with security council directives.
Islamists oppose the proposal which they see as a threat to the role of religious schools, which students can attend only after completing state education.
Dealers said technical factors also played a role in the decline after the main market index fell through key support at 1,550 points.
"There was a rapid decline...The market is losing power at a critical point. Positive news is needed to stop this and support the market," said Tuncay Kuzu of Sahin Securities.
Bond yields rose around one percentage point to 98-98.5 percent for long-term paper and to 91-93 pct for short-term paper due to tight liquidity.
Bankers said financial markets concentrated more on a liquidity shortage expected to continue until late April rather than the political problems.

The liquidity shortage was caused by income tax payments and banks' weekend cash needs. Tax payments will continue to drain cash in the first week of April, which will be followed by hefty mid-month public sector salary payments and rising bank cash demand ahead of a four-day Islamic holiday from April 18 to 21.
The Turkish lira firmed to 126,830 against the dollar after closing on Wednesday at 127,110 in line with weakness in the U.S. currency against the mark, dealers said.
($1=126,830 Turkish lira)
